notFormalized.title: Finding 88: the parametrized section at the boundary zeros
notFormalized.label: §5.3, proof of Theorem 5.3.12 (preprint 5.19), p. 222 (preprint p. 180)
notFormalized.book: "Then we consider as before the section $(\lambda, x) \mapsto f(x) + \sum\lambda_is_i(x)$, and, for a generic value of $\lambda$ ... the associated section $s_\lambda$ has the desired properties."
notFormalized.instead: **Checked on paper only.** At a zero $(0, x)$, $x \in \partial X$, where all $s_i$ vanish, $\ker F'(0, x) = \mathbb R^m \times \ker f'(x)$ is in good position to $\mathbb R^m \times C_x$ only if $\ker f'(x) + E_x \supseteq T_xX$, a general position condition that good position does not imply ($\mathbb R(1, 1)$ in $[0, \infty)^2$). So "as before" cannot apply Theorem 3.6.8 (preprint 3.54) to $F$ there; the formal proof avoids these points (V5.40) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 88).

notFormalized.title: Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21)
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Remark 5.3.14 (preprint 5.21), p. 223 (preprint p. 181)
notFormalized.book: Instead of $(f|X_i, P|Y_i) = (f_i, P_i)$ one should require that the problems are isomorphic and make this part of the data.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** Definition 5.3.13 (preprint 5.20) takes the restrictions to $t^{-1}(0)$, $t^{-1}(1)$ as the end problems (V5.41) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 100).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22): Morse-type structure
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Theorem 5.3.15 (preprint 5.22), p. 223 (preprint p. 181) (proof pp. 223–228 (preprint pp. 181–186))
notFormalized.book: For a generalized compact homotopy with end problems in general position and $\partial X = X_0 \sqcup X_1$, an arbitrarily small $s_0 \in \Gamma^{+,1}_U(P)$ vanishing near $\partial X$ makes $(f + s_0, x)$ in general position at every zero and $t : S_{f+s_0} \to [0, 1]$ a function with only Morse-type critical points.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs finite-dimensional Morse theory on manifolds with boundary, the cotangent bundle of the solution set, a parametric Sard theorem and a trivialization $\Phi_\lambda : S \to S_\lambda$ of the family (not "the classical standard implicit function theorem"); its proof also needs $dt(x) \ne 0$ at the critical points of $t|S$, which the preprint and 2017 statements do not assume (V5.42); the 2021 Definition 5.3.13 (3) asks $dt(x)$ onto at every smooth point and so supplies it (`lemma_5_3_16_2021`, V5.69), but the theorem itself is still not formalized. Lemmas 5.3.16, 5.3.17 (preprint 5.23, 5.24) are V5.42–V5.44 (Findings, Chapter 5, items 101, 103, 178).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.27 (preprint; not in the 2021 edition): cobordism between good position perturbations
notFormalized.label: §5.3, Theorem 5.27 (preprint), preprint p. 188
notFormalized.book: For a proper homotopy $f_t$ and perturbations $s_0$, $s_1$ putting $f + s_i$ in good position, there is $s(x, t)$ with $s(\cdot, i) = s_i$ such that $f + s$ is in good position at all smooth points; its solution set is a compact manifold with corners meeting $\{i\} \times X$ in $S_0$, $S_1$.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized**: "the proof is left to the reader" (Findings, Chapter 5, item 104).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32): Bonic–Frampton
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32), p. 230 (preprint p. 193)
notFormalized.book: On $L^p$, $\|\cdot\|^p$ is $C^\infty$ for $p$ an even integer, $C^{p-1}$ for $p$ odd, and $C^{[p]}$ for $p$ not an integer.
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized** (cited from [9], Theorem 1, in the 2021 edition from [25]; deep Banach space geometry, not used on the main line; the preprint statement misses "$p$" in (1), (2), which the 2017 and 2021 statements print) (Findings, Chapter 5, items 117, 120, 179).

notFormalized.title: The $L^p$ and Sobolev remark
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), pp. 230–231 (preprint pp. 193–194)
notFormalized.book: The usual norms of $W^{k,p}(\Omega)$ have the differentiability of $\|\cdot\|_{L^p}$; $\beta(\|x\|^p)$ is a bump function of $L^p$; $W^{1,4}(\Omega)$ with $E_m = W^{1+m,4}(\Omega)$ admits sc-smooth bump functions, while for $W^{1,3/2}(\Omega)$ the straightforward one is only sc¹ — "does there exist a sc-smooth bump function on $E$?"
notFormalized.instead: **Not formalized.** It needs Sobolev spaces with their sc-structures (gap G.1) and Theorem 5.5.5 (preprint 5.32) (Findings, Chapter 5, item 118).

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40): Toruńczyk
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.13 (preprint 5.40), p. 234 (preprint p. 198)

notFormalized.title: Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43): Godefroy–Troyanski–Whitfield–Zizler
notFormalized.label: §5.5 (preprint §5.4.2), Theorem 5.5.16 (preprint 5.43), p. 235 (preprint p. 198)
